item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 23, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira exchanged at around N1,330.95 to the US Dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). The official window opened with early spot transactions hovering around N1,330.95 to N1,332.00 per dollar, maintaining relative stability following recent daily fluctuations. In the unofficial parallel market, street traders and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across major commercial hubs, including Lagos and Abuja, quoted buying rates around N1,360 to N1,365 per dollar, while selling rates traded between N1,375 and N1,380 per dollar. The gap between the official NFEM rate and the parallel market continues to reflect ongoing demand from retail buyers, small business importers, and individuals seeking foreign currency for international travel and tuition payments. At current trading levels, exchanging $100 yields approximately N133,095 through official banking and NFEM channels, compared to up to N138,000 when purchased through parallel market operators. Market participants attribute current rate stability to sustained diaspora remittance inflows alongside foreign portfolio interest in domestic yield instruments. item.title: NYSC kidnap: DSS witness exposes how suspects were identified
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — A Department of State Services, DSS, operative yesterday told an Imo State High Court how 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members were abducted at gunpoint while travelling to orientation camps, as hearing began in the case against three alleged kidnappers. The witness, Ikechukwu Emmanuel, who investigated the incident, said the victims and one of the bus drivers identified the three defendants during an identification parade. The defendants, Usman Aliyu, alias Chonge; Babangida Aliyu; and Mohamed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper, are standing trial on a three-count charge of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms in suit number HOU/22C/2026. Testifying before Justice Emeka Orafu, the DSS operative said the incident occurred at about 6.30am on October 1, 2026, when the 20 prospective corps members were travelling in two buses from Ibadan to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. He told the court that armed men wielding AK-47 rifles attacked the buses and took all 20 passengers hostage, moving them into the bush. According to the witness, security agencies in Imo State, including the DSS, launched operations using human and technical intelligence to track the kidnappers and secure the victims’ release. He said the hostages were eventually released after the payment of ransom demanded by the kidnappers, while investigations continued. Emmanuel further told the court that intelligence reports indicated that the suspects had moved to Rivers and Abia states, leading to their arrest between October 10 and 14, 2026. Explaining the identification process, the witness said the three defendants were placed among 10 other persons during an identification parade. He said the abducted prospective corps members and one of the bus drivers identified them. The witness also told the court that Usman Aliyu, in his confessional statement, said 11 persons participated in the kidnap operation. The Imo State Director of Public Prosecutions, Mr Martins Udolwu, led the prosecution team, while Mr Nnaemeka S.C. Adipo and Mr Paschal Ofoma represented the defendants. After the witness’s evidence-in-chief, Justice Orafu adjourned the case to October 27, 28 and 29, 2026, for continuation of hearing. The judge urged the defence to be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately after the conclusion of his evidence-in-chief, stressing that he did not want the trial to extend into the new year. “The Defence must be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately he is done with his evidence in chief,” the judge said. item.title: Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has died at the age of 57 following a brief illness, his family has announced. The family announced his death in a statement posted on the actor’s official Instagram page in the early hours of Friday, expressing appreciation to fans and well-wishers for their prayers and support. “We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. “We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen,” the statement read. Duru is survived by his wife, Adokiye, and children Duru, who began his acting career in 1989, became widely known for his role as Ahanna in Rattlesnake , the 1995 film produced by the late filmmaker Amaka Igwe. His death comes months after he dismissed reports that he was battling a life-threatening illness, describing footage circulating online in June as false. In a video posted on Instagram in response to the reports, the actor rejected claims about his health and criticised those circulating the footage. Born on July 27, 1969, in Cameroon to Nigerian parents from Imo State, Duru completed his primary and secondary education in Cameroon before moving to Nigeria for university studies. He studied Theatre Arts at the University of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1996. Duru made his film debut in Missing Mark in 1989, in a production directed by the late Ndubuisi Oko. His performance in Rattlesnake later established him as a recognised face in Nollywood. Over his decades-long career, he featured in several Nigerian films, including Blood Money (1997), Stigma (2013) and Mboputa (2020). In 2020, he won the Best Actor in a Leading Role (Igbo) award at the Best of Nollywood Awards for his performance in Mboputa . He also received the United Nations Ambassador of Peace award in 2007 in recognition of his influence on young people. Duru served as interim president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria in 2010 and was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role at the Africa Movie Academy Awards that year. The lawmaker urged residents to support the proposed state police system, saying improved security would enable farmers to return to their farms and harvest their produce without fear of kidnapping. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Ali Pate who spoke, expressing optimism that she could recover fully. But the minister failed to respond on the number of contacts under high-risk or whether any of the 46 contacts have tested positive for the virus. He however, insisted that government would not take anything for granted despite the absence of evidence of community transmission. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, had on Wedneday, directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to place the 46 contacts on a no-fly list, comprising 44 persons who came into contact with the patient at a hospital after she developed symptoms and two members of her domestic staff. Keyamo, in a statement on his verified X account following a virtual meeting with Pate, said he had also directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to notify domestic and international airlines of the restriction. The measure is intended to prevent the contacts from travelling by air during the period within which symptoms may develop following exposure. The minister said efforts are ongoing to isolate the individuals pending confirmation that they had not been infected. He also ordered heightened Ebola surveillance at international airports, including temperature checks, travel history monitoring, digital health declarations and stronger coordination with public health authorities. Speaking at a briefing in Abuja, Pate said the patient’s travel history indicated that the case was imported. She was reportedly asymptomatic on arrival in Nigeria but developed symptoms days later. He said contact tracing had covered people at the hospital where she received treatment, her domestic contacts and a private medical facility she had visited. High-risk contacts have been placed in quarantine at a designated facility, while other contacts are being monitored in line with public health guidelines. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, has activated its incident management system in collaboration with the Federal Capital Territory Administration. “I spoke with the clinicians today, and I understand that the laboratory results show significant improvement. There is a possibility that she will recover fully. However, we cannot take anything for granted. “We currently have one confirmed case, and our priority is to contain it and prevent transmission into communities or a wider outbreak,” he said. The government has informed state governments and directed those yet to complete their Ebola response plans to do so urgently. Additional resources have also been mobilised to strengthen the NCDC’s capacity, while the Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats has stepped up coordination. Chairman of the task force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said Nigeria’s surveillance system enabled early identification of the case. Gbajabiamila said the patient had no symptoms when she arrived in Abuja, with the symptoms emerging four days later. He attributed the detection to protocols put in place by the Health Ministry, the task force and other agencies. He assured Nigerians that the task force would strengthen existing protocols and ensure more rigorous enforcement, urging citizens to cooperate with public health authorities. Africa CDC seeks travel history Meanwhile, Director-General of the Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr. Jean Kaseya, said the patient was born in Uganda and called for full disclosure of her travel history to help establish where she contracted the virus. Speaking on Channels Television’s Morning Brief, Kaseya said the woman travelled to Uganda, where she spent some days before her husband joined her. He said the couple returned to Abuja on October 3. He said African health authorities are working together to determine whether the infection originated in Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo or another location. “What we want is collaboration from this lady. She has to tell us, to disclose to the authorities; I need this information, Nigeria needs this information because we need also to support Uganda,” Kaseya said. His comments came amid differing accounts from Nigerian and Ugandan authorities over the patient’s nationality and travel history. Uganda’s health authorities had said the woman is Nigerian and had travelled to eastern DRC for business before transiting through Uganda. Uganda’s Director-General of Health Services, Charles Olaro, maintained that travelling through Uganda did not establish that the infection was contracted there, adding that the location of exposure remains under investigation. Kaseya also explained that no vaccine is currently available for the Bundibugyo strain responsible for the outbreak, although clinical trials of candidate vaccines, including one manufactured in Egypt, had commenced. He criticised what he described as inadequate global investment in developing vaccines for diseases predominantly affecting Africa, arguing that international partners needed to support vaccine research and development more urgently. Tomori said: “The government must be completely transparent about matters like this. We don’t want to hear information in bits and pieces from different sources.” He called for clearer information about the patient’s movements, the extent of contact tracing and the handling of diagnostic samples, while acknowledging that certain medical details might need to remain confidential. The breakdown of food inflation by state shows that Lagos recorded the highest food inflation, at 34.40 per cent, on a year-on-year basis, followed by Imo at 33.79 per cent and Ondo at 31.49 per cent. On the other hand, three northern states recorded the slowest rises in food inflation on a year-on-year basis, with Taraba recording a negative 7.47 per cent, Yobe a negative 0.37 per cent and Borno a negative 2.18 per cent. A Vanguard market survey carried out at Mile 12 International Market, one of the biggest foodstuff markets in Lagos, on some food items between August, September and October reflects price swings in items such as tomatoes, fresh onions, fresh pepper, beans, yam, plantain and sweet potatoes, while the prices of rice, horse mackerel (Titus), palm oil and guinea corn remained the same. Farmers’ groups react Deputy National President of the All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN), Mr. Daniel Okafor, blamed the high cost of fuel and poor roads, which he said had increased transportation and logistics expenses. item.description: … Say Nigeria’s Mental Health Act needs action, not just legislation By Chioma Obinna Nigeria and other African countries must invest in home-grown mental health research and translate policies into action to improve care for millions of people facing mental health challenges, psychiatrists have said. The experts warned that Africa’s low contribution to global mental health research was limiting the continent’s capacity to develop evidence-based responses suited to its population, while weak implementation of policies threatened to widen the gap between legislation and access to care. They spoke at the ninth International Research Conference of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Lagos, themed, “Mental Health Research at the Crossroads: Challenges, Policies and Reforms in Africa.” Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, a professor of psychiatry at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, said Africa accounted for less than two per cent of global mental health research output, a situation he said underscored the urgent need to strengthen local research capacity. Sheikh called for increased investment in African-led studies, arguing that research priorities should reflect the realities of local communities and provide evidence for policies and interventions. He also drew attention to the implementation gap surrounding Nigeria’s Mental Health Act, stressing that the existence of a law was not enough without concrete action, institutional commitment and adequate resources. The Medical Director of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Dr Olugbenga Owoeye, said research was essential to improving clinical practice and strengthening the delivery of mental health services. item.title: FG powers 2,214 homes, businesses with Kano mini-grids
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has commissioned two solar mini-grids in Kano State, providing 2,214 electricity connections to homes and businesses in underserved communities. The projects, delivered through the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) under the Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES) programme of the Nigeria Electrification Project (NEP), are funded by the World Bank. Located in Ballagaza, Gabasawa Local Government Area, and Marayar Rogo, Warawa Local Government Area, the facilities have a combined installed capacity of 268.4 kilowatt-peak (kWp). A statement by the REA on Thursday said the Ballagaza mini-grid has a capacity of 195.2kWp, while the Marayar Rogo facility has 73.2kWp. The projects have provided 1,564 electricity connections in Ballagaza and 650 in Marayar Rogo. Speaking at the commissioning, the Minister of Power, Chief Joseph Tegbe, said the projects demonstrated the importance of investment in renewable energy and collaboration with the private sector in expanding electricity access. He said the Federal Government would continue to encourage partnerships that accelerate the delivery of reliable and sustainable electricity, particularly to rural communities. According to him, the projects would bring electricity closer to underserved populations, support small businesses and create an enabling environment for economic growth. The REA said the mini-grids were expected to support productive activities, including milling, welding, tailoring, cold storage and other commercial services, improving business operations, productivity and household incomes. Representing Kano State Governor, the Managing Director of the Kano State Rural Electricity Board, Abba Kabir Yusuf, commended the Federal Government and the REA for extending electricity infrastructure to the benefiting communities. He said improved electricity supply would support commercial activities, enhance productivity and contribute to the state’s socio-economic development. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the REA, Abba Abubakar Aliyu, said the agency’s objective went beyond installing electricity infrastructure to ensuring that communities derived tangible economic benefits from the projects. “With 2,214 connections across Ballagaza and Marayar Rogo, we are creating opportunities for households, supporting local businesses and providing a dependable foundation for productive work, stronger enterprises and improved incomes,” Aliyu said. Girls, children with disabilities and those in underserved communities must be among the first to benefit.” The Nigeria Learning Passport, one of the programme’s major platforms, provides online, mobile and offline access to curriculum-aligned educational resources for pre-primary, primary and secondary school pupils. The platform hosts more than 15,000 educational resources, including lessons in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba. It has recorded more than 2.5 million registered students and nearly 100,000 registered teachers. The initiative, introduced in Nigeria during the COVID-19 pandemic when school closures disrupted learning nationwide, is now hosted by the Federal Ministry of Education as part of efforts to expand access to educational resources. Through the partnership, Airtel provides zero-rated access to the Nigeria Learning Passport, the ministry’s Inspire and Ignite platforms, the Digital National Education Management Information System and the Youth Agency Marketplace, also known as YOMA. The arrangement allows users to access the designated platforms without incurring mobile data charges, addressing one of the major obstacles to digital learning for families with limited resources. Head of Programmes at the Airtel Africa Foundation, Esi Asare Prah, said digital inclusion in education was central to preparing young Africans for an increasingly technology-driven world. “One of the biggest missions for the foundation is driving faster digital inclusion in education to improve learning outcomes,” Prah said. “For Airtel as an organisation, digital inclusion is a major priority. item.title: CAP backs lead poisoning prevention, promotes safer paint practices
item.description: One of Nigeria’s leading paint and coatings manufacturers, Chemical and Allied Products, CAP, Plc, has urged Nigerians to prioritise product safety when choosing paint, saying products used in homes, schools and workplaces should contribute to healthier environments. CAP also called on manufacturers, retailers, painters and building professionals to promote responsible product selection and support efforts to prevent lead exposure across Nigeria. The call coincides with International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week, ILPPW, 2026, observed from October 18 to 24, with the theme: ‘From Detection to Prevention’. The global campaign highlights the importance of identifying sources of lead exposure and strengthening preventive measures to protect public health, particularly among children. Lead exposure remains a significant public health concern. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), there is no known safe level of lead exposure. Lead can affect multiple body systems, with children particularly vulnerable to its effects on brain development, learning and behaviour. Exposure can occur through several sources, including lead-containing paint, particularly when painted surfaces deteriorate or are disturbed during renovation. Commenting on the importance of paint safety, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of CAP Plc, Olalekan Aluko, said: “When choosing paint, people naturally consider the colour, the finish and the cost. These are important, but safety deserves the same attention. The products used in our homes, schools and workplaces should contribute to healthier environments for the people who live, learn and work in them. “At CAP Plc, our commitment to paint solutions formulated with no added lead goes hand in hand with our responsibility to promote better practices across the industry. Preventing lead exposure is a shared responsibility. Manufacturers, regulators, retailers, painters, building professionals and consumers all have a role to play, from ensuring product safety and providing reliable information to making informed decisions about the products used in our homes and workplaces.” Through its Painters Academy, CAP Plc also supports efforts to educate painters on paint safety and responsible product selection, equipping them to make informed recommendations to customers. The academy has trained more than 8,000 painters across 17 states. Through its ongoing partnership with the National Business and Technical Examinations Board, NABTEB, CAP Plc also supports the professionalisation of painting and pathways to recognised qualifications. item.title: Judge gives Trump Dec. 11 deadline to testify in BBC lawsuit
item.description: A US judge on Thursday issued President Donald Trump a December 11 deadline to testify under oath in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC. Judge Enjolique Lett in Miami gave the order in response to complaints by the British broadcaster that Trump has refused to sit for a deposition, including canceling a previously agreed date of October 16. If Trump fails to attend the deposition by then, he risks sanctions, including dismissal of his lawsuit, the court said. Trump has accused the BBC of deceptively editing its documentary “Trump: A Second Chance” to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters to march on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, after losing the presidential election. The crowd proceeded to storm Congress in an attempt to stop the formal certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s victory. While the BBC has apologized for the incident, which prompted the resignation of multiple senior executives, the broadcaster has denied it caused Trump any real injury and moved for the case to be dismissed. Trump filed his suit against the BBC in December 2025 and is seeking at least $5 billion on each of two counts. Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC, said in court that Trump had no real excuse not to testify and that on October 16, he had only been campaigning, “participating in party politics.” “No plaintiff is above the law,” Tobin said. In a court filing Wednesday, Trump’s legal team argued that he was not seeking to avoid a deposition but had been constrained by “matters of national importance.” The lawyers said Trump would be able to give a deposition between January 11 and 22. Trump has made attacks on the media a signature of his two presidential terms, insulting reporters who ask questions he doesn’t like and seeking to ban outlets airing critical reports from the White House. Most recently, the administration has plunged into a legal dispute with CNN, MSNOW and Politico over attempts to bar them from the White House. With his approval ratings in the low 30 percent range and polls showing his Republican Party likely to lose control of the House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections, Trump faces increasing headwinds as he approaches his final years in power. item.title: N10bn untouched – APC accuses Atiku of politicising Ebola response
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President, Atiku Abubakar, of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, insisting that approved emergency funds remain untouched. The council’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. Alake said President Bola Tinubu approved N10 billion for the Ebola emergency in June, but relevant agencies deployed other available resources. “On accountability, the Atiku camp should note that the N10 billion the President approved for the Ebola emergency in June remains untouched,” he said. He said the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and other agencies strengthened surveillance at entry points. According to him, the surveillance network alerted the government to the index case and facilitated contact tracing for 44 contacts. The council commended the agencies for their contributions to monitoring the Ebola threat and supporting the public health response. It also criticised Atiku’s reference linking President Tinubu’s name to Ebola, saying it risked turning a serious health concern into political ridicule. “We believe linking and rhyming President Bola Tinubu’s name to Ebola only risks turning a serious health concern into a vehicle to ridicule the President,” Alake said. The council also defended the handling of the infected Nigerian’s detection, citing the virus’s incubation period and the timing of symptoms. “For anyone infected with the virus, the incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, with symptoms typically appearing eight to 10 days after exposure. “An infected person cannot spread or transmit Ebola to others until they actively develop symptoms,” he said. Alake urged opposition politicians to support health authorities rather than criticise the government’s response to the public health threat. “A responsible opposition will applaud the Task Force for being responsive. But the Atiku camp always goes for cheap shots at the government,” he said. The council also rejected Atiku’s allegation that a ministerial briefing was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies or voting. Alake described the allegation as speculative, adding that the briefing instead urged Nigerians to comply with protocols announced by the task force. He called on Atiku and his supporters to avoid politicising public health concerns, urging Nigerians to shun rumours and follow health authorities’ guidance. “We advise Atiku Abubakar and his hirelings to avoid politicising public health issues,” he said. The council said protecting Nigerians from the deadly disease should remain the priority. item.title: Tinubu names former DSS DG Bichi NISS board chairman
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appointed former Director-General of the Department of State Services, Yusuf Bichi, as Chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies. The appointment was announced in a statement issued on Thursday by the institute’s Director of Coordination and Liaison, Lilian Omo-Odigwe, and published through the DSS’s X account. According to the statement, Bichi’s appointment followed a recommendation by the incumbent DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Ajayi. “The Commander-In-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, has approved the appointment of Y. M. Bichi, CFR, FWC, the immediate past Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), as Chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS), Lower Usuma Dam, Abuja.” The statement added, “Bichi’s appointment was approved by President Tinubu based on the recommendation of the current DG-DSS, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi.” Bichi’s appointment took effect on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and will run for an initial four-year term. “His appointment is for an initial four-year term, effective 22nd October, 2026, in accordance with Section 4 of the National Institute for Security Studies (Establishment) Act, 2019,” the statement said. He succeeds A.A. Gadzama as chairman of the institute’s governing board. Bichi previously led the DSS before handing over to Ajayi in August 2024. “Bichi, who will succeed A.A. Gadzama, OFR, mni, on the Governing Board, handed over leadership of the DSS to the incumbent Director-General in August 2024,” the statement added. Bichi began his career in the Security Division of the Kano State Cabinet Office before his transfer of service in 1984. The institute said his appointment would bring “extensive experience in intelligence, security administration, operational leadership and institutional training to the governance of the National Institute”. item.title: We sought Aso Rock venue because APC uses it too – Sowore
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has defended his party’s request to hold the inauguration of its 2027 Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, arguing that opposition parties should enjoy the same access as the ruling All Progressives Congress. Sowore made the remarks on Thursday at an event organised by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, explaining that the request was prompted by the APC’s use of the facility for political activities. The AAC had written to President Bola Tinubu seeking approval to inaugurate its Presidential Campaign Council at the Villa ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We asked to use Aso Rock because the APC uses Aso Rock to do political party events. So we are saying, as a matter of right, since Aso Rock is our own, other political parties must be granted the opportunity to use Aso Rock the way APC uses Aso Rock,” Sowore said. In addition to the venue, the party requested food, drinks and other logistical arrangements for attendees at the proposed inauguration scheduled for November 11, 2026. A letter dated October 21 and signed by the AAC National Secretary, Oshiokhai Ikpeminioghena, stated that the request was anchored on multiparty democracy, political inclusiveness and equal treatment of political parties. The party maintained that approving the request would affirm the Presidency’s commitment to fairness and demonstrate that public institutions were available to all Nigerians, irrespective of political affiliation. The request triggered a disagreement between Sowore and the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, who criticised the AAC candidate and questioned the party’s electoral strength. Sowore insisted that the move was aimed at securing equal access to the Presidential Villa. He also ruled out joining a proposed opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 elections. “I don’t want to be part of your coalition because your rainbow coalition is going to die after 2027,” he said. item.title: Trump slams LeBron James for national anthem actions
item.description: US President Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behaviour during the playing of the national anthem. Trump posted a video of the basketball legend doing apparent warm-up movements while lined up with his Philadelphia 76ers teammates. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social network. “LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” he wrote. The video used by Trump had an internal caption that read: “LeBron working on his golf swing pregame.” It showed him doing lateral swing motions and basketball shooting movements. It was not immediately clear when the video was filmed. There was no immediate reaction from James, 41, who is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, the 76ers. Trump has been critical of athletes before — particularly Black athletes — for their behaviour during the playing of the US national anthem before games. During his first term, Trump singled out NFL star Colin Kaepernick for his decision to kneel during the “Star-Spangled Banner” to protest racial injustice and police brutality. item.title: Europa League: Bournemouth Hammer 10-Man Milan, Juventus Denied At The Death
item.description: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe’s leading clubs. Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered. Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week. Bournemouth’s Premier League rivals Crystal Palace were held 2-2 by Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo. AC Milan’s Italian defender #33 Davide Bartesaghi reacts after the UEFA Europa League, league stage football match between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium in Bournemouth, southern England on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday. The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games. Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late ‘winner’ ruled out for a marginal offside. Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead. Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike. Rennes’ French goalkeeper #30 Brice Samba speaks with Juventus’ German forward #27 Nick Woltemade at the end of the UEFA Europa League – 1st round day 3 football match between Juventus and Rennes at the Allianz stadium in Turin, on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP) Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland. item.title: 2027 Election: Even Tinubu Knows Atiku Is The Best Candidate – Momodu
item.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communications of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign, Dele Momodu, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as the best candidate for the 2027 election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Momodu said Atiku had been the most deliberate and focused candidate since he first sought the presidency in 1993. The ADC chieftain claimed that President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), also knows that the former vice president is better suited for the job. “When I say he (Atiku) is the best, it is a statement of fact and even President Bola Tinubu himself knows that,” Momodu said. “That is why at a time, he invited him and they joined hands for Atiku to run in the past.” ﻿ Comparing the credentials of the three major presidential candidates, Momodu said Tinubu’s strongest credential was his tenure as governor of Lagos State, while Atiku’s was his experience as vice president and Peter Obi’s as governor of Anambra State. He argued that Tinubu had underestimated the differences between governing Lagos and leading Nigeria. “So, if you look at the three mainstream candidates today, the APC candidate Bola Tinubu, the ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar and the NDC candidate Peter Obi, you can judge for yourself. Bola Tinubu came, his best credential was being the former governor of Lagos State; Atiku came, his best credential was being the former vice president of Nigeria; Peter Obi came, his best credential was being the governor of Anambra State. “So, if you judge for yourself, you will know that perhaps what has happened to President Tinubu is the fact that when he got to the Presidency, he assumed that Nigeria was Lagos and he soon discovered that Nigeria is different from Lagos and that is why he’s had total commotional confusion and his guys are running all over the places throwing money around.” Momodu also accused the Tinubu administration of failing to be sincere with Nigerians, alleging that officials around the President were more concerned with telling him what he wanted to hear than confronting him with the realities facing the country. “What is lacking in this government is that sincerity. Everything is about one man. The people who are running our economy today have to tell Nigerians only what they think the president wants to hear. They are not telling him the truth, and when tomorrow comes, he will realise it,” he added. item.title: Tinubu Tasks Medical Experts On Brain Drain Solutions In West Africa
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged the West African College of Physicians (WACP) to develop practical and sustainable solutions to medical brain drain across the sub-region, warning that the migration of skilled professionals continues to put pressure on healthcare systems. He said the trend limits access to essential medical services and increases the workload on available health personnel. According to a statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu spoke on Thursday after being conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja. He urged the College’s leadership to use its forthcoming conference to develop lasting solutions to the challenge. “We are more challenged in Africa than anywhere else; you know, and with the outbreak of Ebola now we’re looking for a preventive action that will eliminate all these problems and infections. So, I wish you the best. As I pledge to behave myself, I will continue to do whatever I can do for this honourable profession,” the President said. Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to comprehensive health sector reforms aimed at making healthcare delivery more accessible, affordable and efficient for Nigerians. He also commended the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, for driving the reforms. “We as a government are doing everything possible. Please help me congratulate the reform-oriented physician, Ali Pate, who has been doing a very good job,” he said. President Tinubu was conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026.
